name: Salesforce
tagline: A configurable CRM platform to evaluate for customer processes, reporting and cross-team workflows.
description: Salesforce supports configurable CRM workflows; current product scope and independent ratings are not verified here.
pros: A documented sales workflow can be mapped to records, stages and ownership rules.
Complex reporting and automation requirements can be tested before a wider rollout.
A pilot helps reveal data governance and implementation work.
A small pipeline pilot can test ownership, reporting and handoffs.
A documented governance model can reduce long-term configuration drift.
cons: Configuration and ongoing administration can be substantial for complex deployments.
Different products and editions should not be treated as interchangeable.
Migration, integration and renewal scope need written confirmation.

content.title: Define the customer process
content.body: Map the process from lead or enquiry through qualification, opportunity, close and handoff. Include renewals or service if required. Decide which system owns each record and which fields are mandatory before configuring the CRM.

content.title: Configuration and governance
content.body: Test a small set of record types, stages, permissions and automations. Assign owners for changes and establish a review process for fields and rules. Over-customization can create maintenance work and confusing user experiences.

content.title: Data quality and reporting
content.body: Import a controlled sample and test deduplication, ownership, required fields and history. Build the forecast or pipeline report the business actually uses and document definitions. Check that reports remain consistent after a stage or ownership change.

content.title: Integration and access
content.body: List the systems that must exchange customer, product, billing or support data. Test failed syncs and duplicate updates. Review role permissions, audit history, export and offboarding before loading sensitive customer information.

content.title: Implementation and cost
content.body: Request a scoped proposal that separates licenses, implementation, integration, training, support and ongoing administration. Confirm renewal, cancellation and data export terms in writing; current prices and plan limits are not independently verified here.

content.title: Pilot acceptance criteria
content.body: Use a small but representative pipeline with duplicate contacts, reassigned ownership, a stalled opportunity and a close handoff. Verify that reports remain consistent after changes and that users can find the right record without a workaround. Have an administrator and an everyday seller both evaluate the experience.

content.title: Failure cases and governance
content.body: Test an integration retry, a field validation failure, a user who changes teams and an automation that should not fire twice. Document who can change the workflow and how configuration is tested before release. Keep data-quality ownership separate from one-time implementation work.

content.title: Decision record
content.body: Save the scope of products, editions, seats, implementation assumptions, integration ownership, support and renewal terms. List features that were demonstrated versus only described. Revisit the decision if the organization cannot maintain the configuration or the system of record becomes unclear.

faqs.question: Who should evaluate Salesforce?
faqs.answer: Evaluate Salesforce when its primary workflow matches a documented requirement. Test a representative task and verify current capabilities and limits directly with the vendor.

faqs.question: How should a team test Salesforce?
faqs.answer: Use the same real input, expected outcome and acceptance criteria each time. Record pass, partial pass, fail or unknown, including setup time, manual work and failure handling.

faqs.question: Which limitations should be checked in Salesforce?
faqs.answer: Check the exact plan, integrations, permissions, export, data retention, recovery and ongoing administration. Treat untested or undocumented capabilities as unknown until confirmed.

faqs.question: Are Salesforce prices and ratings independently verified here?
faqs.answer: No. Current prices, plan limits and independent ratings are not verified in this review. Check official documentation and obtain a dated quote before purchase.

faqs.question: What should be confirmed before adopting Salesforce?
faqs.answer: Confirm the core workflow, access controls, integrations, data export, account offboarding, support responsibilities and renewal terms. Assign an owner for the implementation and ongoing review.

author: Sarah Chen
learningCurve: Steep — requires dedicated training time for full proficiency
whoShouldUse: Salesforce is designed for fast-growing startups that need a scalable crm & sales platform. Its generous free tier and flexible pricing make it accessible for early-stage companies.
whoShouldNotUse: Salesforce may be overwhelming for users who only need basic crm & sales functionality. Its extensive feature set can create unnecessary complexity for simple use cases.
